newsitem.title: UK: UK store group Heal's to float on stock market.
newsitem.headline: UK store group Heal's to float on stock market.

text.p: Home furnishings retailer Heal's Plc on Tuesday announced it is to float on the London stock market on March 24 following a 14.3 million pound placing of shares.
The shares are being sold at 175 pence, valuing the group at around 1.3 million pounds.
Just over 1.4 million new shares are to be issued and Natwest Ventures and management shareholders are to sell a further 6.7 million existing shares.
The money raised will be invested in developing new products and opening new stores.
The group currently operates three stores - two in London and one in Guildford in southern England.
Heal's chief executive Colin Pilgrim called the flotation a "significant step" in the development of the group.
The company recently spent 1.4 million pounds refurbishing one of its London stores and is keen to take advantage of new site opportunities.
"We have identified a priority list of store locations and whilst our particular store criteria do not make sites easy to find, we would ideally like to open one store a year," said Pilgrim.
In the 53 weeks to September 14, 1996, Heal's reported operating profit before exceptionals of 1.3 million pounds and pre-tax profits of 1.8 million pounds.

In the first twenty weeks of the current year ending February 1, operating profits were 1.5 million pounds. The period historically acccounts for over 90 percent of Heal's profits for the year as a whole.
